text: RetroArch Overlays: Includes your visual overlay configurations and related assets for RetroArch.

title: Device Backup menu - RetroArch Shaders
text: RetroArch Shaders: Preserves your installed shader filters and visual effect presets.

title: Device Backup menu - Save Games + Save States
text: Save Games + Save States: Stores all game saves and save states from RetroArch and other supported emulators.

title: Device Backup menu - Screenshots
text: Screenshots: Backs up all captured screenshots.

title: Device Backup menu - Syncthing Configs
text: Syncthing Configs: Saves the configuration files used by Syncthing for synchronisation between devices.

title: Device Backup menu - System BIOS
text: System BIOS: Includes BIOS files required by some emulators to function correctly. Please Note: these are user supplied should not be distributed.

title: Device Backup menu - Themes
text: Themes: Backs up all installed themes and associated assets used by the frontend.

title: Device Backup menu - User Init Scripts
text: User Init Scripts: Saves any custom user initialisation scripts placed in the MUOS/init folder for execution at startup.

title: Device Backup menu - Backup Target
text: Backup Target: Selects the destination device for storing your backup archive be it SD1, SD2, or attached USB storage.

title: Device Backup menu - Merge Backups
text: Merge Backups: Combines multiple existing backups from different targets into a single unified archive for easier extraction.

title: Device Backup menu - Start Backup
text: Start Backup: Initiates the backup process using the selected items and target. A progress indication will appear during operation, and the archive will be saved to your chosen device target within the BACKUP folder.

title: Colour Options menu
text: Colour options allow you to fine tune how visuals are displayed on the device or within supported content. These adjustments affect overall tone, balance, and clarity, and can be used for comfort, accessibility, or personal preference.

title: Colour Options menu - Temperature
text: Temperature: Adjust colour warmth, shifting the display between cooler and warmer tones.

title: Colour Options menu - Brightness
text: Brightness: Control overall light output, affecting how bright or dim the display appears.

title: Colour Options menu - Contrast
text: Contrast: Change the difference between dark and light areas to improve image definition.

title: Colour Options menu - Saturation
text: Saturation: Increase or decrease colour intensity, from muted tones to more vivid colours.

title: Colour Options menu - Hue Shift
text: Hue Shift: Rotate the colour spectrum, subtly altering overall colour appearance.

title: Colour Options menu - Gamma
text: Gamma: Adjust midtone brightness to fine-tune image balance without overexposing highlights.

title: Colour Filter menu
text: Colour filters adjust how content is displayed by applying visual transformations. These include accessibility focused options for colour blindness and contrast, comfort filters for extended play, and stylistic filters for creative or fun visual effects.

title: Colour Filter menu - None
text: None: No colour filtering applied. Original colours are preserved.

title: Colour Filter menu - Achromatopsia
text: Achromatopsia: Removes colour and increases contrast for users with complete colour blindness.

title: Colour Filter menu - Monochrome
text: Monochrome: Converts the image to grayscale while preserving detail and contrast.

title: Colour Filter menu - Protanopia
text: Protanopia: Adjusts colours to improve visibility for red-cone colour blindness.

title: Colour Filter menu - Deuteranopia
text: Deuteranopia: Adjusts colours to improve visibility for green-cone colour blindness.

title: Colour Filter menu - Tritanopia
text: Tritanopia: Adjusts colours to improve visibility for blue-cone colour blindness.

title: Colour Filter menu - High Contrast
text: High Contrast: Increases overall contrast with deeper blacks and brighter highlights.

title: Colour Filter menu - Blue Light Reduction
text: Blue Light Reduction: Reduces blue intensity to improve comfort in low-light conditions.

title: Colour Filter menu - Warm Tone
text: Warm Tone: Shifts colours toward warmer tones by increasing reds and reducing blues.

title: Colour Filter menu - Cool Tone
text: Cool Tone: Shifts colours toward cooler tones by reducing reds and boosting blues.

title: Colour Filter menu - Sepia Tone
text: Sepia Tone: Applies a warm sepia effect for a classic, vintage appearance.

title: Colour Filter menu - Paper Like
text: Paper Like: Softens colours and contrast to create a paper-like visual style.

title: Colour Filter menu - Mustard
text: Mustard: Applies a warm yellow-heavy tint with subdued blues for a mustard look.

title: Colour Filter menu - Neon Boost
text: Neon Boost: Intensifies colours for a bold, high-saturation neon effect.

title: Colour Filter menu - Toxic Waste
text: Toxic Waste: Pushes vivid greens while suppressing reds and blues for a toxic glow.

title: Colour Filter menu - Vaporwave
text: Vaporwave: Magenta and cyan-heavy palette inspired by retro vaporwave aesthetics.

title: Collection menu
text: The Collection module allows you to organise and group your favourite content into personalised sets. Folders can be created to sort collections by theme, genre, or platform, while individual items can be freely combined across systems. It provides an easy and flexible way to curate and access the content you enjoy most.

title: Collection menu - Collection Folder
text: Collection Folder: Create one level deep folders to keep your collection organised.

title: Collection menu - Collection Item
text: Collection Item: An item that has been collected and stored. Items with the same name can be stored together, along with items from different systems and cores.

title: Configuration menu
text: Where you configure and fine tune every aspect of your device. From connectivity and language to interface design, power management, and backups, each module provides focused control over a specific part of the MustardOS environment. It is the central place to adapt the system to your personal preferences and hardware capabilities.

title: Configuration menu - General Settings
text: General Settings: Change device specific settings, date and time, brightness and volume, hotkeys, and device startup.

title: Configuration menu - Connectivity
text: Connectivity: A central module to connect to Wi-Fi networks and change device specific network settings. A number of web services can also be enabled from here and device specific USB functionality.

title: Configuration menu - Customisation
text: Customisation: Customise the options of various functions within the MustardOS frontend. Catalogue sets, RetroArch configurations, and themes can be downloaded and installed from this module.

title: Configuration menu - Interface Options
text: Interface Options: Customise the look and feel of the MustardOS frontend. Show or hide various options or change how names are displayed through the content explorer.

title: Configuration menu - Colour Options
text: Colour Options: Adjust display colour settings such as temperature, saturation, hue, gamma, and related values where supported either on device or in content only.

title: Configuration menu - Overlay Options
text: Overlay Options: Configure content overlays including the base overlay and battery, volume, and brightness indicators, with options for transparency, position, and scale.

title: Configuration menu - Language
text: Language: Pick a different language for your device. All languages are supported through a Hosted Weblate instance. For all changes, please do so within Weblate and not through our language repository on GitHub.

title: Configuration menu - Power Settings
text: Power Settings: Modify the sleep functionality, low battery indicator, and idle input modes. Idle and default system governors can also be changed within this module.

title: Configuration menu - Storage
text: Storage: Supported devices with an additional mSD slot will allow you to store specific items on a secondary card.

title: Configuration menu - Device Backup
text: Device Backup: A great module to use if you are updating or wanting to share various configurations with another device. Create either individual backups or merge into one big archive for convenience.

title: Connectivity menu
text: The Connectivity module manages how your device interacts with both local and remote networks. From establishing Wi-Fi connections to enabling USB data modes or web based access services, this section centralises all network and connection related functionality.

title: Connectivity menu - Wi-Fi Network
text: Wi-Fi Network: Connect to wireless networks either manually or through previously saved profiles. Supports secure, hidden, and static IP configurations for advanced network setups.

title: Connectivity menu - Network Settings
text: Network Settings: Fine tune how the system handles network detection, module compatibility, and connection recovery. Useful for troubleshooting connection issues or optimising startup behaviour. Typically should be left as default.

title: Connectivity menu - Web Services
text: Web Services: Manage built in network enabled services such as SSH, SFTP, and Syncthing. These tools allow remote access, synchronisation, and system management over an active network connection.

title: Connectivity menu - USB Function
text: USB Function: Switch between ADB (Android Debug Bridge) and MTP (Media Transfer Protocol) modes. ADB provides developer access for debugging and command-line tools, while MTP allows file transfers between the device and a computer.

title: Control Scheme menu
text: Customise how button layouts behave for individual content. The following are predefined schemes so you can match your preferred controller style or preserve authenticity when playing older titles. Each scheme adjusts button orientation and input mapping without affecting the system wide default, including the frontend.

title: Control Scheme menu - Modern
text: Modern: Reconfigures button layout to reflect contemporary console standards, matching common X/Y and A/B placements found on modern controllers. Ideal for players accustomed to newer systems.

title: Control Scheme menu - Retro
text: Retro: Restores classic button positions inspired by retro consoles and handhelds. Perfect for maintaining the original feel of older games.

title: Control Scheme menu - System
text: System: Uses the default global control scheme defined by the system settings. Ensures consistency across all emulators and content unless overridden.

title: Customisation menu
text: Tailor the look, sound, and behaviour of the frontend. From changing themes and fonts to sound effects, these options let you personalise the user experience to your liking. Adjusting these settings affects only the interface and does not alter how content runs or performs.

title: Customisation menu - Catalogue Sets
text: Catalogue Sets: Load and apply user created artwork catalogues that customise how content images and metadata are displayed. These sets can change the overall visual presentation of your library.

title: Customisation menu - RetroArch Configurations
text: RetroArch Configurations: Load custom RetroArch configuration files for finer control over emulator behaviour and performance. Ideal for users who maintain multiple setups or experimental settings.

title: Customisation menu - Theme Picker
text: Theme Picker: Change the appearance of the frontend by selecting from installed themes. You are also able to download themes directly on-device through this option.

title: Customisation menu - Theme Resolution
text: Theme Resolution: Test themes designed for different resolutions or aspect ratios. Useful for validating theme compatibility on various devices or displays.

title: Customisation menu - Theme Scaling
text: Theme Scaling: Scales theme layouts designed for different resolutions to better fit the device screen. Useful for testing themes during creation.

title: Customisation menu - Alternative Theme
text: Alternative Theme: Switch between alternate versions of a theme, such as different colour palettes or layout variants.

title: Customisation menu - Background Music
text: Background Music: Toggles background music in the frontend interface. All music is .ogg and can be switched between Theme based or Global within the MUOS/music folder

title: Customisation menu - Background Music Volume
text: Background Music Volume: Adjust the independent volume of the background music being played. Press A to set.

title: Customisation menu - Black Fade Animation
text: Black Fade Animation: Toggles the fade to black transition animation used when launching content. Disabling this can slightly speed up launch times.

title: Customisation menu - Content Save State Launch
text: Content Save State Launch: Choose between pressing A or holding A to automatically launch the most recent save state for the selected content.

title: Customisation menu - Content Shuffle
text: Content Shuffle: Enables the ability to shuffle through content in the explorer using the R2 button. A fun way to discover random content in your library.

title: Customisation menu - Content Box Art
text: Content Box Art: Changes the display priority of content images, or determining whether box art is shown at all.

title: Customisation menu - Content Box Art Alignment
text: Content Box Art Alignment: Adjusts the position of content images on screen. Useful for theme designers or users wanting a specific layout alignment.

title: Customisation menu - Content Full Width
text: Content Full Width: Toggles whether content highlights use the full screen width or leave space for box art.

title: Customisation menu - Content Launch Splash
text: Content Launch Splash: Toggles the display of a splash image when launching content. Adds a stylish transition or can be disabled for slightly faster load times.

title: Customisation menu - Content Grid Mode
text: Content Grid Mode: Enables grid view mode in the Content Explorer. Display content in a visual grid instead of a list for a more graphical browsing experience.

title: Customisation menu - Hide Grid Mode Box Art
text: Hide Grid Mode Box Art: Hides system box art images when grid mode is active. Useful for simplifying the interface or highlighting custom artwork.

title: Customisation menu - Interface Font Type
text: Interface Font Type: Chooses how fonts are loaded in the frontend. Theme uses fonts included in the theme (with language fallback), while Language forces use of the language-specific font.

title: Customisation menu - Navigation Sound
text: Navigation Sound: Toggles sound effects when navigating the frontend interface. Disabling this results in silent menu movement.

title: Customisation menu - Navigation Sound Volume
text: Navigation Sound Volume: Adjusts the volume level of menu navigation sounds. Press A to set.

title: Customisation menu - Startup Chime
text: Startup Chime: Toggles the chime sound played during frontend startup. A small signal the frontend has finished loading.

title: Danger Settings menu
text: Reserved for the bravest of tinkerers, this section provides direct access to low level system controls that affect storage behaviour, power suspension, and process scheduling. These settings are powerful but risky! Altering them without a clear understanding can impact stability, performance, or data integrity. Adjust only if you know what you are doing or if you like a bit of excitement in your life.

title: Danger Settings menu - Swap Tendency
text: Swap Tendency: Controls how aggressively the system moves inactive memory pages to swap storage. Lower values keep data in RAM longer, improving performance at the cost of higher memory use.

title: Danger Settings menu - Write Back Threshold
text: Write Back Threshold: Defines the percentage of system memory that can contain unwritten (dirty) data before the kernel forces it to be written to disk. Higher values delay writes but risk larger bursts of I/O.

title: Danger Settings menu - Background Write Back
text: Background Write Back: Sets the memory percentage that triggers background write-back activity. Lower values reduce latency by keeping storage more up-to-date but may increase write frequency.

title: Danger Settings menu - Cache Reclamation
text: Cache Reclamation: Determines how aggressively the kernel reclaims cached file data. Higher values free cache space quickly, while lower values improve access times for frequently used files.

title: Danger Settings menu - I/O Merge Policy
text: I/O Merge Policy: Configures how the kernel merges adjacent I/O requests into single operations. Disabling merges may improve responsiveness on flash storage with low latency.

title: Danger Settings menu - Queue Depth
text: Queue Depth: Sets the maximum number of pending I/O operations allowed per device. Higher values increase throughput for heavy workloads but also raise memory usage.

title: Danger Settings menu - Read Ahead Size
text: Read Ahead Size: Specifies how much data the kernel preloads before an application requests it. Larger read-ahead values benefit sequential reads, while smaller ones suit random access patterns.

title: Danger Settings menu - Swap Read-Ahead
text: Swap Read-Ahead: Defines how many memory pages are prefetched from swap during reads. Lower values reduce latency; higher values improve performance for sustained swap activity.

title: Danger Settings menu - Realtime Timeslice
text: Realtime Timeslice: Determines how long real time tasks can run before being rescheduled. Lower values enhance responsiveness, while higher values favour long, continuous processing.

title: Danger Settings menu - I/O Stats
text: I/O Stats: Enables or disables kernel level tracking of per-device I/O statistics. Disabling this feature can slightly improve performance by reducing overhead.

title: Danger Settings menu - Idle Flush Mode
text: Idle Flush Mode: When enabled, the system flushes dirty data during idle periods instead of waiting for write thresholds. Useful for flash storage and reducing power draw while inactive.

title: Danger Settings menu - Fork Optimisation
text: Fork Optimisation: Prioritises newly created (forked) processes to run before their parent. Can improve perceived load times in some applications.

title: Danger Settings menu - Scheduler Scaling
text: Scheduler Scaling: Adjusts kernel scheduler behaviour dynamically based on CPU core count. Disabling this keeps tuning consistent across multi-core and single-core systems.

title: Danger Settings menu - Disk Tuning
text: Disk Tuning: Switches between predefined disk or card performance profiles. Useful for optimising behaviour on specific SD cards or external storage.

title: Danger Settings menu - Suspend Power State
text: Suspend Power State: Changes how the system enters and resumes from sleep mode. Different suspend states balance between faster wake-up and lower idle power consumption.

title: Device Settings menu
text: Configure highly specific device level options and integrations. These settings control deep system behaviour and hardware communication. These should NOT be changed unless instructed to do so by a MustardOS developer, as improper modification may affect system stability or functionality.

title: Device Settings menu - Bluetooth Integration
text: Bluetooth Integration: Indicates whether Bluetooth hardware is present and supported for wireless peripherals or audio devices.

title: Device Settings menu - RGB LED Integration
text: RGB LED Integration: Displays whether the system includes controllable RGB lights, used primarily by themes.

title: Device Settings menu - Kernel Level DebugFS
text: Kernel Level DebugFS: Shows if a debug system is available in the kernel, allowing low level inspection of system internals and device behaviour. This should always be enabled unless a specific device does not have this functionality.

title: Device Settings menu - HDMI Integration
text: HDMI Integration: Indicates whether HDMI output is available and functioning, used for connecting to external displays.

title: Device Settings menu - Lid Switch Integration
text: Lid Switch Integration: Displays whether the device supports a lid or sleep switch to automatically suspend upon closure of device lid.

title: Device Settings menu - Network Integration
text: Network Integration: Shows whether network interfaces such as Wi-Fi or Ethernet are detected and integrated within the system.

title: Device Settings menu - PortMaster Support
text: PortMaster Support: Indicates whether PortMaster is installed and functional, allowing direct access to downloadable ports, applications, and other community content.

title: Governor menu
text: Assign a specific CPU governor to individual content. A CPU governor controls how the processor adjusts its frequency in response to workload, balancing performance, power consumption, and heat output. The selected governor is change when the content is launched, then restores the system default once it exits. These options are derived from the standard Linux CPU frequency scaling subsystem and availability may vary depending on your device. For more information please see the CPU Governors and How Do They Work FAQ page.

title: Governor menu - Ondemand
text: Ondemand: Dynamically scales CPU speed based on system load. Provides a strong balance between performance and efficiency. Ideal for most games and applications.

title: Governor menu - Performance
text: Performance: Locks the CPU to its highest possible frequency. Ensures maximum performance at the cost of higher power draw and increased heat.

title: Governor menu - Powersave
text: Powersave: Keeps the CPU fixed at its lowest possible frequency. Great for conserving battery life or reducing heat during light workloads.

title: Governor menu - Conservative
text: Conservative: Similar to Ondemand but changes frequency more gradually, avoiding sudden spikes or drops. Provides smoother performance transitions at slightly lower responsiveness.

title: Governor menu - Interactive
text: Interactive: Ramps CPU frequency up quickly when activity is detected. Favourable for input heavy applications but can cause sudden power spikes on slower hardware.

title: Governor menu - Schedutil
text: Schedutil: Integrates with the Linux scheduler to make real time frequency decisions based on task priority. Offers the best overall balance on newer multi core devices.

title: Governor menu - Userspace
text: Userspace: Enables manual control of CPU speed through system tools like SSH or ADB. Intended for advanced users who want precise frequency tuning.

title: HDMI Settings menu
text: Configure video and audio output for external displays. Adjust resolution, colour settings, and audio routing to achieve the best possible image and sound when connecting the device via HDMI. These settings may vary depending on the devices hardware capabilities and the display being used.

title: HDMI Settings menu - Resolution
text: Resolution: Selects the output resolution for HDMI display, ranging from 480p to 720p depending on device support. Higher resolutions provide sharper visuals but may increase power usage. Due to technical limitations 1080p is currently unavailable as a resolution.

title: HDMI Settings menu - Colour Space
text: Colour Space: Defines the colour encoding standard used for HDMI output. Choose between RGB for full digital precision or YUV values for improved compatibility with certain displays.

title: HDMI Settings menu - Colour Depth
text: Colour Depth: Sets the number of bits used to represent colour per channel, such as 8-bit or 10-bit. Higher bit depths allow for smoother gradients and more accurate colour reproduction.

title: HDMI Settings menu - Colour Range
text: Colour Range: Determines the output range of the RGB colour space. Full range outputs all colour levels (0–255), while Limited range (16–235) may be required for certain televisions or monitors.

title: HDMI Settings menu - Scan Scale
text: Scan Scale: Adjusts the screen scaling between overscan and underscan to ensure the entire image fits properly on the display. Use this if parts of the picture appear cropped or there are black borders.

title: HDMI Settings menu - Audio Output
text: Audio Output: Selects whether audio is played through the devices internal speakers or routed to the connected display.

title: History menu
text: The History module provides a quick way to revisit content you have recently played. It helps you track previously launched items, identify those saved to collections, and resume from where you left off. This section is ideal for quickly continuing your gameplay or reviewing recent activity without browsing through your full library.

title: History menu - Previously Played Content
text: Previously Played Content: Quickly launch previously played content or add the item to a collection.

title: History menu - Content within a Collection
text: Content within a Collection: A star is indicative of content that has been added to one or more collections.

title: Information menu
text: The Information Menu brings together all system details, diagnostics, and reference tools in one place. From checking storage capacity and input functionality to viewing hardware statistics, network data, and credits, this section provides insight into both the technical and community sides of MustardOS.

title: Information menu - Community News
text: Community News: Stay up to date with official announcements, feature highlights, and community driven updates. News items are curated directly from the MustardOS Community Forum , keeping you informed about development progress, releases, and notable contributions.

title: Information menu - Activity Tracker
text: Activity Tracker: View detailed statistics about how content is played. Track play time, launch counts, play styles, and view long term trends to better understand your personal play/usage habits.

title: Information menu - Screenshots
text: Screenshots: View all the screenshots that have been taken on the device. These are specific to MustardOS and not screenshots from RetroArch or images. This is not a general image viewer.

title: Information menu - Storage Space
text: Storage Space: View the current used space of the mounted storage devices as well as the internal storage.

title: Information menu - Input Tester
text: Input Tester: Test the various controls on the device to ensure they are working and mapped properly.

title: Information menu - System Details
text: System Details: Access version information and details about the CPU, memory, temperature, and battery info. The frontend can also be refreshed directly from here if any changes were made manually.

title: Information menu - Network Details
text: Network Details: Access network information like IP and MAC addresses, Wi-Fi signal range, traffic throughput and more. You are also able to change the hostname and randomise the MAC address when not connected to a network.

title: Information menu - Supporters and Credits
text: Supporters and Credits: View all of the current MustardOS developers, supporters, and contributors. Along with some awesome music to watch it with.

title: Kiosk Settings menu
text: Restrict or permit specific areas of MustardOS. It is primarily used for shared environments, kid modes, or simplified user modes. Options within this menu define which functions, modules, and applications remain accessible while the device is locked in kiosk mode.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Kiosk Mode
text: Kiosk Mode: Enables or disables kiosk mode, locking the system into a restricted state with only approved functions available.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Restricted Messages
text: Restricted Messages: Displays or hides warning messages when attempting to access restricted features while in kiosk mode.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Archive Manager
text: Archive Manager: Allows or restricts access to the Archive Manager for installing or managing specific created MustardOS archives.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Task Toolkit
text: Task Toolkit: Determines whether maintenance, diagnostic, and recovery tools can be accessed.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Customisation
text: Customisation: Toggles access to theme, catalogue, and other visual or functional customisation features.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Language
text: Language: Controls whether users can change the system language while in kiosk mode.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Wi-Fi Network
text: Wi-Fi Network: Allows or blocks access to wireless network management and configuration.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Storage
text: Storage: Defines whether users can sync or migrate their user data across from primary to secondary storage.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Backup
text: Backup: Controls access to the user data backup functionality.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Network Settings
text: Network Settings: Toggles access to advanced network configuration options.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Web Services
text: Web Services: Enables or disables access to background web services.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Content Core
text: Content Core: Determines if users can change default emulator cores used for launching content.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Content Governor
text: Content Governor: Allows or restricts the ability to adjust CPU governors for individual content launches.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Content Control Scheme
text: Content Control Scheme: Controls access to remapping controller layouts for specific content.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Content Options
text: Content Options: Toggles ability to access additional content settings such as cores, governors, control schemes, and tags.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - RetroArch Kiosk
text: RetroArch Kiosk: Locks RetroArch into a kiosk safe configuration with limited access to settings and menus.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Content Search
text: Content Search: Enables or disables search functionality within the content explorer.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Content Tag
text: Content Tag: Determines whether users can attach content tags to their content.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Custom Catalogue
text: Custom Catalogue: Allows or blocks the use of custom catalogue sets for curated content.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Custom RetroArch Configs
text: Custom RetroArch Configs: Toggles access to user defined RetroArch configuration profiles.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Custom Themes
text: Custom Themes: Controls whether new visual themes can be applied.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Theme Download
text: Theme Download: Allows or restricts downloading themes directly from the online MustardOS repository.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Date and Time
text: Date and Time: Determines if users can adjust system time and date while kiosk mode is active.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Timezone
text: Timezone: Controls whether timezone settings can be changed.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Applications
text: Applications: Enables or disables launching installed applications while kiosk mode is active.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Configuration
text: Configuration: Restricts or permits access to global configuration menus and general settings.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Content Explorer
text: Content Explorer: Allows or blocks navigation through the main content library.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Collection Viewing
text: Collection Viewing: Determines whether collections can be viewed while kiosk mode is enabled.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Collection Adding Content
text: Collection Adding Content: Allows or prevents users from adding new content to collections.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Collection Folder Creation
text: Collection Folder Creation: Controls the ability to create new collection folders.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Collection Removal
text: Collection Removal: Toggles permission to delete or remove items from collections.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Collection Access
text: Collection Access: If a folder called kiosk is created as a folder name, enabling this will use that specific folder for a curated collection. Allows you to have two completely separate collections.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - History Viewing
text: History Viewing: Controls visibility of the launch history list.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - History Removal
text: History Removal: Allows or prevents clearing history entries.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Information
text: Information: Toggles access to system information menus such as storage, network, and device status.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Advanced Settings
text: Advanced Settings: Determines whether expert level configuration options can be viewed or changed.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - General Settings
text: General Settings: Allows or restricts access to general settings such as brightness, sound, and hotkeys.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - HDMI Settings
text: HDMI Settings: Controls access to display output and HDMI configuration options.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Power Settings
text: Power Settings: Determines whether power management features such as sleep and idle modes can be modified.

title: Kiosk Settings menu - Interface Options
text: Interface Options: Allows or blocks access to interface visibility, theme layout, and menu style options.

title: Language menu
text: Select your preferred language for the MustardOS interface. All translations are community-driven and maintained through Weblate . Changing the language affects the frontend menu and interface text only. It does not alter emulator or game language settings.

title: Language menu - Language Option
text: Language Option: Switch between available language packs installed on your device. You can update translations on-device by pressing the X button when an active network connection is available.

title: Main Menu menu
text: The Main Menu is the central starting area for MustardOS, providing quick access to all core features and utilities. From exploring your content and managing collections to checking system information or adjusting configuration settings, every essential function begins here. It serves as the primary entry point for navigating and operating your device.

title: Main Menu menu - Explore Content
text: Explore Content: Access and browse your content stored across SD1, SD2, or USB devices. This is the primary area for launching content and exploring the next amazing title. Don't forget that you can organise your content in any named folder that you like.

title: Main Menu menu - Collection
text: Collection: View, organise, and manage your curated collections of favourite titles. Create themed or personalised sets for quick access to your most played or most loved content.

title: Main Menu menu - History
text: History: Quickly revisit content that was recently launched or accessed. The history log makes it easy to jump back into your last session without needing to go back and finding it manually.

title: Main Menu menu - Applications
text: Applications: Browse and launch installed applications, tools, and system utilities. This section includes both built-in MustardOS apps and any compatible third party programs you have added.

title: Main Menu menu - Information
text: Information: Display detailed system information including version and build details, network status, and device diagnostics. Ideal for checking up on performance or verifying technical details at a glance.

title: Main Menu menu - Configuration
text: Configuration: Configure and customise how your device behaves and looks. Adjust interface layouts, tweak functionality, and refine general preferences to match how you want your device to act and feel.

title: Main Menu menu - Reboot
text: Reboot: Safely restart the device without performing a full shutdown. Useful after configuration changes or manual updates to ensure a clean system state.

title: Main Menu menu - Shutdown
text: Shutdown: Power down the system cleanly and securely. This ensures that all running processes and mounted storage devices are safely unmounted before the system turns off. Please be patient and wait before removing any storage devices.

title: Main Menu menu - Kiosk Settings
text: Kiosk Settings: Configure kiosk for device specific restrictions, limiting access to certain features when the device is locked for shared use, or typically for younger players, or if you would like to see less.

title: Network Settings menu
text: The Network Settings module provides fine control over how the system handles wireless and wired network connections during startup, compatibility checks, and recovery. These options are primarily useful for troubleshooting various network issues, managing module loading behaviour, and improving reliability across different hardware configurations.

title: Network Settings menu - Connection Monitor
text: Connection Monitor: Enables periodic connectivity checks and automatically triggers reconnection if the network connection is lost. Useful for maintaining stable connections in environments with inconsistent Wi-Fi signal strength.

title: Network Settings menu - Start Network on Boot
text: Start Network on Boot: Automatically starts the network connection during system boot. This ensures connectivity is available as soon as the device powers on without requiring manual activation.

title: Network Settings menu - Start Network on Wake
text: Start Network on Wake: Re-connects the Wi-Fi network connection after the device resumes from sleep. Useful for ensuring background services and online features reconnect automatically after waking.

title: Network Settings menu - Module Compatibility
text: Module Compatibility: Enables compatibility mode for network module loading through the Linux kernel. This improves support for certain Wi-Fi chipsets but can moderately increase boot times.

title: Network Settings menu - Module Async Load
text: Module Async Load: Loads compatible network modules asynchronously in the background. This option significantly reduces boot times when Module Compatibility is enabled and should only be disabled if troubleshooting connection failures.

title: Network Settings menu - Module Wait Time
text: Module Wait Time: Sets the maximum time the system will wait for the network interface to appear during boot. Increasing this value may improve stability on slower devices but will extend startup time. Avoid adjusting if Module Compatibility is already enabled, as both delays will compound.

title: Network Settings menu - Module Retry
text: Module Retry: Determines how many times the system will attempt to load the network module when using Module Compatibility mode. Increasing this value can help with unstable or delayed network drivers, but may extend overall boot duration.

title: Network Details menu
text: The Network Details module provides a full overview of your current network configuration and connectivity status. It includes information about your hostname, IP and MAC addresses, connected access point, and traffic statistics. This section is useful for troubleshooting network issues, checking connection quality, or managing device identity when connecting to different networks.

title: Network Details menu - Hostname
text: Hostname: Displays the current hostname used to identify your device on the network. This can be changed from within the module if required, but only when the network is not actively connected.

title: Network Details menu - MAC Address
text: MAC Address: Shows the hardware level MAC address assigned to the network interface. It can also be randomised when disconnected for privacy, but only when the network is not actively connected.

title: Network Details menu - IP Address
text: IP Address: Displays the current address assigned to the device by your router or access point.

title: Network Details menu - Access Point
text: Access Point: Indicates the SSID of the wireless network your device is currently connected to.

title: Network Details menu - Gateway
text: Gateway: Displays the network gateway or router address responsible for managing external connections.

title: Network Details menu - DNS
text: DNS: Lists the DNS servers currently in use for resolving internet domain names.

title: Network Details menu - Signal
text: Signal: Shows the current network signal strength, providing an indication of connection quality and range.

title: Network Details menu - Channel
text: Channel: Displays the wireless channel number, and specific frequency, used by the connected access point, useful for interference troubleshooting.

title: Network Details menu - Accumulated Traffic
text: Accumulated Traffic: Shows the total amount of data transmitted and received since the network connection was established.

title: Network Details menu - Throughput Traffic
text: Throughput Traffic: Displays real time upload and download speeds for monitoring active network performance.

title: Wi-Fi Network menu
text: Configure Wi-Fi and network connection details. These options provide full control over authentication, addressing, and connection behaviour—useful for networks that do not broadcast automatically or require specific parameters such as static IPs or private DNS servers.

title: Wi-Fi Network menu - Identifier
text: Identifier: The SSID or name of the wireless network you wish to connect to. This identifies the access point and must match exactly, especially for hidden or secured networks. You can also press X to scan for networks.

title: Wi-Fi Network menu - Password
text: Password: The password, or security key, required to join the selected wireless network. Leave blank for open networks that do not require authentication.

title: Wi-Fi Network menu - Hidden Network
text: Hidden Network: Enables connection to a network that does not broadcast its SSID. When enabled, the device will attempt to connect even if the network is not visible in scans.

title: Wi-Fi Network menu - Network Type
text: Network Type: Defines the connection mode for the network. Typically set to DHCP for automatic configuration, or Static for advanced users specifying static IP settings.

title: Wi-Fi Network menu - Device IP
text: Device IP: The IP address assigned to the device when using manual configuration. This defines the unique address on the network and must not conflict with other devices.

title: Wi-Fi Network menu - Subnet CIDR
text: Subnet CIDR: Specifies the network subnet mask in CIDR notation. This determines the range of valid IP addresses within the local network.

title: Wi-Fi Network menu - Gateway IP
text: Gateway IP: The IP address of the network gateway or router used to access external connections. Required for internet access when using manual network settings.

title: Wi-Fi Network menu - DNS Server
text: DNS Server: Defines the Domain Name System (DNS) server address used to resolve website and service names. You may specify a local DNS server or a public one such as 1.1.1.1 (Cloudflare) or 8.8.8.8 (Google).

title: Wi-Fi Network menu - Connect
text: Connect: Initiates connection to the configured network using the provided credentials and settings. Press it again to disconnect the device from the network. Press Y to save the current network to a profile.

title: Content Option menu
text: The Content Options menu allows you to view and modify detailed information for any selected item within the Content Explorer. From checking play statistics to assigning emulator cores and adjusting performance governors, this section provides everything needed to fine tune how individual content behaves when launched.

title: Content Option menu - Directory
text: Directory: Displays the full folder path of the selected content, showing where the file is located within your storage.

title: Content Option menu - Name
text: Name: The display name of the content item. This can differ from the file name depending on how the content was scanned or renamed.

title: Content Option menu - Time Played
text: Time Played: Shows the total cumulative time the content has been played. This helps track usage and identify your most frequently played items.

title: Content Option menu - Times Launched
text: Times Launched: Displays how many times this content has been launched. Ideal for tracking play frequency.

title: Content Option menu - Search
text: Search: Opens the search interface to locate similar or related content. Helpful for finding alternate versions or other entries in a series.

title: Content Option menu - Core
text: Core: Assigns the specific emulator system and core that will be used to launch this content.

title: Content Option menu - Governor
text: Governor: Sets the CPU governor profile for this content. Allows you to optimise between performance and battery efficiency on a per title basis.

title: Content Option menu - Control Scheme
text: Control Scheme: Customise the button layout and control scheme for this content. Perfect for titles requiring non standard input configurations or comfort adjustments.

title: Content Option menu - Threaded Video
text: Threaded Video: Toggle RetroArch threaded video support to improve performance on supported systems.

title: Content Option menu - Remove Config
text: Remove Config: Remove RetroArch configuration files per content, core, or directory.

title: Content Option menu - Colour Filter
text: Colour Filter: Apply accessibility and stylistic colour filters, including monochrome and colour blind modes. This works for most, if not all, RetroArch content.

title: Content Option menu - Glyph Tag
text: Glyph Tag: Assign a custom glyph or tag icon to the content. These icons appear next to content within the Content Explorer, helping visually distinguish special items or categories.

title: Overlay Options menu
text: Overlay options control how on-screen indicators and base overlays are displayed whilst playing content. These settings allow fine adjustment of visibility, placement, and size for the content base overlay and other indicators such as low battery, volume, and brightness.

title: Overlay Options menu - Content Base Transparency
text: Content Base Transparency: Adjusts the opacity of the base overlay shown whilst playing content.

title: Overlay Options menu - Content Base Position
text: Content Base Position: Sets the on-screen position of the content base overlay.

title: Overlay Options menu - Content Base Scale
text: Content Base Scale: Controls the size of the content base overlay.

title: Overlay Options menu - Low Battery Transparency
text: Low Battery Transparency: Adjusts the opacity of the low battery warning overlay.

title: Overlay Options menu - Low Battery Position
text: Low Battery Position: Sets the on-screen position of the low battery indicator.

title: Overlay Options menu - Low Battery Scale
text: Low Battery Scale: Controls the size of the low battery indicator.

title: Overlay Options menu - Volume Transparency
text: Volume Transparency: Adjusts the opacity of the volume level indicator.

title: Overlay Options menu - Volume Position
text: Volume Position: Sets the on-screen position of the volume indicator.

title: Overlay Options menu - Volume Scale
text: Volume Scale: Controls the size of the volume indicator.

title: Overlay Options menu - Brightness Transparency
text: Brightness Transparency: Adjusts the opacity of the brightness level indicator.

title: Overlay Options menu - Brightness Position
text: Brightness Position: Sets the on-screen position of the brightness indicator.

title: Overlay Options menu - Brightness Scale
text: Brightness Scale: Controls the size of the brightness indicator.

title: Theme Picker menu
text: Browse, install, and organise visual themes that change the overall look and feel of the MustardOS frontend. Themes control everything from background images and icons to colour palettes and font styles, allowing you to personalise the interface to match your taste or device aesthetic.

title: Theme Picker menu - Theme Download
text: Theme Download: Download additional themes directly when an active connection is available. This expands your available selection without needing to install themes manually.

title: Theme Picker menu - Folder
text: Folder: Organise themes into folders for easier navigation. Each folder can hold multiple themes, helping you sort them by creator, style, or even resolution.

title: Theme Picker menu - Theme
text: Theme: Select and install a compatible theme. Once applied, it will update the appearance of menus, backgrounds, and the general interface elements throughout the MustardOS frontend.

title: Explore Content menu
text: The Content Explorer is where all playable and viewable content is displayed. It automatically merges all mounted storage devices and presents folders and content in an organised way. Each item includes visual indicators showing whether it has been played before, is part of a collection, or is ready for launch through an assigned core.

title: Explore Content menu - Content Folder
text: Content Folder: Displays folders containing compatible content. MustardOS does not enforce strict naming conventions, allowing you to name and structure your folders however you prefer, including nested folders for organisation.

title: Explore Content menu - Content File
text: Content File: Represents an individual content file, such as a game or media item. Files are automatically launched with their assigned system or emulator core, or you will be prompted to select one if no association exists.

title: Explore Content menu - Previously Played (History)
text: Previously Played (History): Indicates content that has been launched before. This helps you quickly identify items with existing play history for easy access or relaunching.

title: Explore Content menu - In Collection
text: In Collection: Marked content that has been added to one or more collections. These items remain accessible in both their original folder and any collection they belong to. This can be toggled in Interface Settings.

title: Power Settings menu
text: The Power Settings module allows you to control how MustardOS manages power, performance, and idle behaviour. These settings define what happens when the device is left inactive, reaches low battery levels, or enters sleep mode. You are also able to switch how the CPU behaves under normal and idle conditions, helping balance performance with battery life.

title: Power Settings menu - Sleep Function
text: Sleep Function: Toggle between several options that changes how the power button acts when the device is powered on. Shutdown after a period of time during sleep, instant shutdown, or keep the device powered on until the power button is pressed again.

title: Power Settings menu - Low Battery Indicator
text: Low Battery Indicator: Toggles the LED/RGB light behaviour when the battery reaches a critically low level.

title: Power Settings menu - Idle Input Sleep Timeout
text: Idle Input Sleep Timeout: Sets how long the device remains idle before automatically entering sleep mode.

title: Power Settings menu - Idle Input Display Timeout
text: Idle Input Display Timeout: Defines the duration of inactivity before the display automatically turns off to conserve energy.

title: Power Settings menu - Mute on Display Timeout
text: Mute on Display Timeout: Automatically mutes system audio when the display turns off due to inactivity.

title: Power Settings menu - Idle Governor
text: Idle Governor: Determines which CPU governor is applied during the idle display timeout.

title: Power Settings menu - Default Governor
text: Default Governor: Sets the CPU governor used during normal device operation.

title: Power Settings menu - Frontend Screensaver
text: Frontend Screensaver: Enables or disables the frontend screensaver when the idle display timeout is reached.

title: Date and Time menu
text: Manually adjust the system clock and calendar settings used with the frontend, emulators, and applications alike. These controls ensure accurate timestamps for files, logs, and saved data even without network access.

title: Date and Time menu - Set Timezone
text: Set Timezone: Opens the Timezone selection module, where you can set the correct regional timezone for your country or area. Ensures automatic adjustment for daylight saving time and proper alignment with your local region.

title: Date and Time menu - Year
text: Year: Adjusts the current system year.

title: Date and Time menu - Month
text: Month: Changes the system month value.

title: Date and Time menu - Day
text: Day: Sets the current calendar day.

title: Date and Time menu - Hour
text: Hour: Adjusts the system clock hour value.

title: Date and Time menu - Minute
text: Minute: Sets the minute portion of the system time.

title: Date and Time menu - Time Notation
text: Time Notation: Switch between 12 hour and 24 hour time formats. This setting changes how time is displayed in the frontend.

title: Search menu
text: Quickly find your content across all storage. Whether you are looking within a single folder or across every connected storage device, this tool helps you locate specific content without having to browse manually.

title: Search menu - Lookup
text: Lookup: Enter the name or partial name of the content you wish to find. Searches are not case sensitive.

title: Search menu - Search Local
text: Search Local: Performs a search within the currently selected folder and all subfolders. Useful when you know roughly where the file is stored but not its exact name.

title: Search menu - Search Global
text: Search Global: Searches across all currently mounted and active storage devices, including SD1, SD2, and USB. Ideal for locating content when you're unsure which device or directory it resides in.

title: Screenshots menu
text: The Screenshot Viewer displays all captured images taken through MustardOS. It allows you to browse, preview, and manage your screenshots directly from the device. Use the available controls to navigate, hide the menu for an unobstructed view, or delete unwanted captures with ease.

title: Screenshots menu - Screenshot Image
text: Screenshot Image: The screenshot image that you have taken. Pressing the A button will hide the menu allowing you to still navigate up and down the list of screenshots. Using the X button will remove the screenshot from the device.

title: Storage Space menu
text: The Storage Information module provides an overview of all detected storage devices connected to your system. It lists primary, secondary, external, and internal storage areas, showing how each is used within MustardOS. Monitoring available space here helps maintain system stability and ensures your data and applications have room to operate smoothly.

title: Storage Space menu - Primary Storage
text: Primary Storage: Typically the first, and sometimes only , user data storage mount on the device.

title: Storage Space menu - Secondary Storage
text: Secondary Storage: Some devices come with a secondary storage option allowing you to use it for both content and MustardOS settings.

title: Storage Space menu - External Storage
text: External Storage: If a device has a USB connection you may be able to mount it via the storage mount Task Toolkit scripts.

title: Storage Space menu - System Storage
text: System Storage: Internal storage, or the RootFS as we call it , is where most important data is held. It is always a good idea to keep a watch on this as a typically full system storage may cause issues.

title: Storage menu
text: Relocate key user data from SD1 to SD2, if your device supports a secondary card. This ensures that personal data such as saves, themes, configurations, and collections remain intact even if SD1 needs to be reformatted or reflashed. Using this feature helps protect against data loss and simplifies both maintenance and updates.

title: Storage menu - Applications
text: Applications: Moves user installed applications and their data to SD2, ensuring they remain accessible after reflashing SD1.

title: Storage menu - System BIOS
text: System BIOS: Migrates user supplied system BIOS files used by emulators to SD2 for safer storage.

title: Storage menu - Metadata Catalogue
text: Metadata Catalogue: Transfers box art, grid icons, splash screens, and text metadata to SD2, keeping your content visuals intact.

title: Storage menu - Content Collection
text: Content Collection: Moves all content collection data, preserving your curated lists and favourites.

title: Storage menu - History
text: History: Relocates your play history and recently launched items so these remain consistent after SD1 reflash.

title: Storage menu - User Init Scripts
text: User Init Scripts: Transfers user initialisation scripts from MUOS/init folder, ensuring custom startup routines persist.

title: Storage menu - Background Music
text: Background Music: Moves your chosen background music tracks for the frontend to SD2, preserving your personalised theme audio.

title: Storage menu - Friendly Name System
text: Friendly Name System: Migrates your friendly name configuration files to SD2, maintaining cleaned up or renamed content titles.

title: Storage menu - Network Profiles
text: Network Profiles: Moves saved Wi-Fi profiles and credentials, reducing the need to reconnect manually after reinstallation.

title: Storage menu - Custom Packages
text: Custom Packages: Transfers user created packages such as catalogue sets and RetroArch configuration packages to secondary storage.

title: Storage menu - Save Games + Save States
text: Save Games + Save States: Moves RetroArch and emulator save files and states to SD2, keeping gameplay progress safe and sound.

title: Storage menu - Screenshots
text: Screenshots: Migrates all screenshots taken on the device to SD2, ensuring those precious "retro" achievements remain even after updates.

title: Storage menu - Syncthing Configs
text: Syncthing Configs: Moves Syncthing configuration data, preserving sync configuration and paired device settings.

title: Storage menu - Themes
text: Themes: Relocates installed frontend themes and associated assets, preventing awful loss during SD1 reflash. However do keep in mind that future updates may break theme compatibility.

title: Storage menu - Activity Tracker
text: Activity Tracker: Moves your playtime tracking and session data files to SD2, maintaining usage records after any reflash.

title: System Details menu
text: The System Details module provides a realtime view of the device current status and specifications. It displays software and hardware information such as version, build ID, kernel, CPU statistics, and memory usage, along with power, temperature, and uptime details. This section is useful for monitoring system performance or confirming device information after updates and configuration changes.

title: System Details menu - Version
text: Version: Displays the current MustardOS version installed on the device.

title: System Details menu - Build ID
text: Build ID: Shows the unique identifier for the installed build, useful for verifying update versions and support requests.

title: System Details menu - Device Type
text: Device Type: Indicates the model and hardware variant of the device.

title: System Details menu - Linux Kernel
text: Linux Kernel: Displays the Linux kernel version that the device is currently using.

title: System Details menu - System Uptime
text: System Uptime: Shows how long the device has been running since the last boot or restart.

title: System Details menu - CPU Information
text: CPU Information: Displays the CPU model, and architecture, detected by the system.

title: System Details menu - CPU Speed
text: CPU Speed: Shows the current operating frequency, in MHz , of the CPU in real time.

title: System Details menu - CPU Governor
text: CPU Governor: Indicates the active CPU scaling governor, which controls performance and power efficiency.

title: System Details menu - System Memory
text: System Memory: Displays the total available RAM and current memory usage of the device.

title: System Details menu - Temperature
text: Temperature: Shows the current operating temperature of the device, usually measured from the CPU sensor.

title: System Details menu - Battery Capacity
text: Battery Capacity: Displays the remaining battery percentage based on live current readings.

title: System Details menu - Battery Voltage
text: Battery Voltage: Indicates the current battery voltage, useful for diagnosing power or charging issues.

title: System Details menu - Charger
text: Charger: Indicates if the device is currently being actively charged.

title: System Details menu - Reload Frontend
text: Reload Frontend: Manually reload the frontend to apply any configuration or theme changes made outside of the interface.

title: System Details menu - Device Settings
text: Device Settings: Configure very specific device functionality, options within here should not be changed unless otherwise told to do so by a MustardOS developer.

title: Glyph Tag menu
text: Assign alternative visual icons to your content, helping you quickly identify special attributes or personal categories in your library. Tags can mark progress, status, or content type. Think of these glyphs as tiny visual notes for how you view or use your content.

title: Glyph Tag menu - Abandoned
text: Abandoned: Mark content that you started but decided not to finish. A subtle reminder that some adventures are best left behind...

title: Glyph Tag menu - Alternate
text: Alternate: Used for different versions of the same content. Great for distinguishing between regional releases or enhanced editions.

title: Glyph Tag menu - Backlog
text: Backlog: Tag items you plan to play later. Keeps your " to play " list visible without too much noise.

title: Glyph Tag menu - Complected
text: Complected: The content is complected, what more do you want?

title: Glyph Tag menu - Completed
text: Completed: Marks content that has been fully finished or cleared. Useful for tracking progress across long campaigns.

title: Glyph Tag menu - Cursed
text: Cursed: For content that causes chaos, crashes, or confusion. Use sparingly, or proudly, depending on your temperament.

title: Glyph Tag menu - Experimental
text: Experimental: Indicates prototypes, test builds, or early versions. Perfect for tinkerers who like to live dangerously.

title: Glyph Tag menu - Homebrew
text: Homebrew: Designates community made or unofficial content. Highlights independent creativity within your collection.

title: Glyph Tag menu - In Progress
text: In Progress: Marks content that you're currently playing or testing. A helpful visual cue for ongoing sessions.

title: Glyph Tag menu - None
text: None: Removes any previously assigned glyph and returns the content to its default untagged state.

title: Glyph Tag menu - Patched
text: Patched: Used for content that has been modified or fixed with community or developer patches.

title: Glyph Tag menu - Replay
text: Replay: For content worth revisiting... whether for achievements, nostalgia, or perfectionism!

title: Glyph Tag menu - Romhack
text: Romhack: Identify content that has been altered or expanded from their original versions. Excellent for modded or fan edited experiences.

title: Glyph Tag menu - Translated
text: Translated: Denotes content that has been localised or fan translated into another language. Perfect for tracking imported or previously inaccessible titles.

title: Task Toolkit menu
text: The Task Toolkit provides a collection of maintenance and recovery utilities designed to keep your system healthy and organised. From clearing caches and restoring essential files to managing storage devices and generating diagnostic reports, it serves as a go to area for troubleshooting.

title: Task Toolkit menu - Clear Tasks
text: Clear Tasks: Quickly clear the catalogue, collections, history, system cache and other items if you are having issues. This is usually the first section to use when troubleshooting various issues.

title: Task Toolkit menu - Restore Tasks
text: Restore Tasks: Various tasks that will help restore specific system files, structure, or content within the MustardOS system.

title: Task Toolkit menu - Storage Tasks
text: Storage Tasks: This section will allow you to safely eject and mount secondary and USB external storage.

title: Task Toolkit menu - System Diagnostics
text: System Diagnostics: Running this script will created a compressed archive that you can send to MustardOS developers to help diagnose issues with both hardware and software.

title: Timezone menu
text: Select the correct regional timezone for your device. This ensures that the displayed system time, file timestamps, and scheduled operations match your local region and daylight saving rules.

title: Timezone menu - Timezone Region
text: Timezone Region: Sets the timezone for your current country or region. This determines how the system clock adjusts automatically for daylight saving changes and ensures timestamps align with your local time.

title: Advanced Settings menu
text: Access to deeper configuration options that affect system behaviour, user experience, and hardware control. These options are designed for experienced users beyond typical settings. Adjusting some of these values may impact stability or device behaviour, so proceed carefully.

title: Advanced Settings menu - Menu Acceleration
text: Menu Acceleration: Adjusts how quickly menu navigation accelerates when holding down directional buttons. Higher values make scrolling faster, while lower values provide more precise control.

title: Advanced Settings menu - Menu Repeat Delay
text: Menu Repeat Delay: Determines how long a button must be held before it begins repeating its action. Increasing this delay can help prevent accidental repeated inputs when navigating menus.

title: Advanced Settings menu - Battery Offset
text: Battery Offset: Applies a correction value to the displayed battery percentage. Useful for calibrating the battery indicator if readings are consistently higher or lower than expected.

title: Advanced Settings menu - Button Swap
text: Button Swap: Globally switches button layouts across the system. Ideal for users preferring alternate control schemes or region specific button arrangements.

title: Advanced Settings menu - Menu Navigation
text: Menu Navigation: Choose between different navigation modes to suit preferred menu control styles.

title: Advanced Settings menu - Volume On Boot
text: Volume On Boot: Sets the default system volume level each time the device starts. Useful for ensuring consistent audio behaviour after reboots.

title: Advanced Settings menu - Brightness On Boot
text: Brightness On Boot: Defines the display brightness applied automatically when the system starts. Adjust this to maintain a comfortable default viewing level on every boot.

title: Advanced Settings menu - Thermal Zone Control
text: Thermal Zone Control: Toggles automatic thermal protection that safely powers down the device when overheating. Disabling this is not recommended as it prevents the system from responding to high temperature warnings.

title: Advanced Settings menu - Passcode Lock
text: Passcode Lock: Enables a passcode requirement for device startup, launching content, or other features.

title: Advanced Settings menu - LED During Play
text: LED During Play: Toggles the device’s power LED visibility while launching or running content. Useful for reducing distractions during gameplay or conserving minor power.

title: Advanced Settings menu - Random Theme on Boot
text: Random Theme on Boot: Automatically selects and applies a random theme each time the device boots.

title: Advanced Settings menu - RetroArch Network Wait
text: RetroArch Network Wait: Delays RetroArch startup until a network connection is detected. Primarily used for features like RetroAchievements that require online access before launch.

title: Advanced Settings menu - RetroArch Config Freedom
text: RetroArch Config Freedom: Removes system enforced configuration restrictions on RetroArch. Allows advanced users to manually customise RetroArch behaviour, but may cause instability if misconfigured.

title: Advanced Settings menu - RetroArch Startup Cache
text: RetroArch Startup Cache: Caches RetroArch and its libraries at boot for faster launches, at the cost of slightly longer startup time.

title: Advanced Settings menu - Activity Tracker
text: Activity Tracker: Toggles content activity tracking and statistics collection.

title: Advanced Settings menu - Device Rumble
text: Device Rumble: Enables or disables vibration feedback for events such as startup, sleep, and shutdown. Enhances tactile feedback where supported by hardware.

title: Advanced Settings menu - User Init Scripts
text: User Init Scripts: Controls the execution of user defined startup scripts. When enabled, the system will run shell ( .sh ) scripts stored in the MUOS/init directory during boot.

title: Advanced Settings menu - DPAD Swap Function
text: DPAD Swap Function: Toggles the DPAD swap feature, allowing directional input remapping through a designated hotkey combination.

title: Advanced Settings menu - Audio Overdrive
text: Audio Overdrive: Extends maximum system audio output from 100% to 200%, providing additional loudness when required. Use carefully, as excessive volume may cause speaker distortion or hardware strain.

title: Advanced Settings menu - Device Lid Switch
text: Device Lid Switch: Enables automatic sleep functionality when closing or opening a physical lid switch, if supported by the device.

title: Advanced Settings menu - Display Suspend
text: Display Suspend: Toggles the display suspend behaviour when the device enters sleep mode. Some display panels may not resume correctly if this setting is enabled, so use with caution.

title: Advanced Settings menu - System Swapfile
text: System Swapfile: Configures the system’s swapfile usage, allowing limited expansion of virtual memory. Useful for memory intensive content or testing system performance under load.

title: Advanced Settings menu - System ZRam
text: System ZRam: Uses compressed RAM as swap space, providing faster memory expansion without disk access.

title: Advanced Settings menu - Secondary Partition
text: Secondary Partition: Specifies which partition number the system should mount when accessing secondary storage. Typically used for advanced configurations or multi partitioned mSD cards.

title: Advanced Settings menu - External Partition
text: External Partition: Sets the partition number used when mounting external USB storage devices. Adjust this if the system fails to detect or mount certain external drives correctly.

title: Advanced Settings menu - Brightness Increment
text: Brightness Increment: Defines how much the screen brightness changes per adjustment step. Smaller increments provide finer control, while larger ones allow quicker adjustments.

title: Advanced Settings menu - Volume Increment
text: Volume Increment: Adjusts how much the volume level changes per input step. Ideal for tuning audio to your specific preference.

title: Advanced Settings menu - GPU Performance Mode
text: GPU Performance Mode: Push the onboard GPU to the maximum frequency at all times. Only on supported devices.

title: Advanced Settings menu - Audio Subsystem Wait
text: Audio Subsystem Wait: Toggle if the device will wait for the audio subsystem to initialise during boot. May increase boot time by a few extra seconds.

title: Advanced Settings menu - Audio Reverse
text: Audio Reverse: Swaps left and right audio channels for the internal speaker output.

title: General Settings menu
text: The General Settings module provides access to a variety of essential system options that define how the device behaves and interacts with connected hardware. These settings cover display output, input responsiveness, and system behaviour at startup. Most adjustments here are safe for everyday use and allow you to fine tune your general experience.

title: General Settings menu - Date and Time
text: Date and Time: Adjust the systems current date, time, and timezone. Accurate timekeeping helps ensure proper logging, updates, and synchronisation with network services. Not to forget that some content also requires proper time being set.

title: General Settings menu - HDMI Settings
text: HDMI Settings: Configure video output options for HDMI capable devices, including resolution, scaling, and other preferences.

title: General Settings menu - Advanced Settings
text: Advanced Settings: Contains specialised system controls intended for advanced users or developers. Changes here can affect hardware behaviour, so proceed with caution.

title: General Settings menu - Brightness
text: Brightness: Adjust the display brightness to a comfortable level. Lower brightness can help conserve power, while higher levels improve outdoor visibility.

title: General Settings menu - Volume
text: Volume: Set the master volume level for all sounds, including menus, games, and notifications.

title: General Settings menu - Device RGB Lights
text: Device RGB Lights: Enable or disable the devices RGB lighting system, adjusting visual effects and theme integration.

title: General Settings menu - DPAD Swap Hotkey
text: DPAD Swap Hotkey: Configure which button combination toggles the DPAD swap function, useful for adjusting control layouts in certain games or emulators. This option only appears for specific devices without analogue sticks.

title: General Settings menu - Screenshot Hotkey
text: Screenshot Hotkey: Set the preferred button combination for capturing screenshots quickly during gameplay or navigation.

title: General Settings menu - Device Startup
